description: ThinkRail is the agentic IDE that gets better every time you use it
summary: The spec-graph and reusable-skills layer is the interesting part here: instead of re-deriving project context every session, ThinkRail persists structured knowledge so the underlying `pi` agent actually accumulates understanding of your codebase, which lands closer to the observability-and-trust problem I care about than another "AI pair programmer" pitch. The git-worktree workspace isolation is also a clean pattern for parallel agent sessions — each agent gets its own branch and working directory, you merge what you want and discard the rest — and it's the same multi-session routing problem I'm solving in PenguPool, just wrapped in a heavier JetBrains-style IDE shell with a keyboard model I actually enjoy. I'll be watching how the extension system lands, because an agent that can author its own tools on demand is the composability story I want to see proven outside a single vendor's ecosystem.
